rationale: Applied P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE (cancel superseded/stale runs). The workflow is triggered by both schedule and workflow_dispatch on the same branch, so overlapping runs can consume runner time for the same smoke-test check. Adding a top-level concurrency group keyed by workflow and ref with cancel-in-progress cancels the older in-progress run when a newer revision starts, while the newest run always completes to preserve build/test coverage. The change is minimal: it adds no new permissions, secrets, network access, or deployment/publishing steps, and leaves all existing jobs, steps, timeouts, environment settings, and required checks intact. Preconditions are met (same workflow+branch grouping; newer run supersedes older). The release/deployment contraindication was assessed as not applying because this is a verification smoke test on a development environment rather than an actual deployment, and cancel-in-progress leaves the latest run to finish.
